title: BA1/2326/2023 of UTTAM KUMAR Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
First Bail Application No. 2326 of 2023
Uttam Kumar ........Applicant

Present:-
Mr. Parikshit Saini, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. Vipul Painuli, Brief Holder for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 Applicant Uttam Kumar is in judicial custody
in FIR/Case Crime No.145 of 2023, dated 28.06.2023,
under Sections 387, 120-B IPC, Police Station Khanpur,
District Haridwar. He has sought his release on bail.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. According to the FIR, on 27.06.2023, at
01:40 PM, the informant received a call from a specified
number. The caller introduced himself as Goldy Brard
and demanded `20 Lakhs or else threatened the
informant to his life.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would
submit that in order to make it the case of extortion
delivery has to be made otherwise, it is not a complete

2
offence. He would submit that the mobile number from
which the call was made, as recorded in the FIR has no
connection with the applicant; that SIM has never been
recovered from him; the informant in his subsequent
statement had revealed two other phone numbers, from
which, he received calls, but that is an improvisation
and there has been no call details, as such.
5. Learned State counsel would submit that the
informant was given life threatening calls and
demanded money and one of the mobile number was
recovered from the applicant.
6. It is the stage of bail. Much of the discussion at
this stage is to be avoided. To the extent of appreciating
the controversy the matter may be examined with the
caveat that any observation made at this stage shall
have no bearing at any subsequent stage of the case.
7. It is true that in order to make out the case of
extortion delivery is must. But, there are cases of
attempted extortion, as well, which are punishable
under Sections 385, 387, 389 IPC, which has also been
held by the Hon'ble Madhya Pradesh High Court in the
case of Sudha Tripathi vs. State of M.P. and others,

3
MANU/MP/0443, 2019. In para 5.12, the Hon'ble Court
observed as hereunder:-
"5.12. The offence in question of extortion is a
serious offence which is considered to be graver than theft
but not as graver as robbery. However, the seriousness of
the offence of extortion, is evident from the very fact that
attempt to commit extortion is separately punishable u/S.
385, 387 and 389 of IPC."
8. In the instant case, it is true that the number
from which, according to the FIR, call was made to the
informant has not been procured as yet, but the
informant has given subsequent statement to the
Investigating Officer that there have been two other
telephone numbers from which he received threatening
calls and demand of money was made. As per
prosecution, one of the mobile numbers ending with
684 was recovered from the applicant.
9. Creating terror in the society and demanding
money under the threat of life are really very serious
offences in a civilized society. There are links which
connect the applicant to the offence.

4
10. Having considered, this Court is of the view
that it is not a case fit for bail and the bail application
of the applicant deserves to be rejected.
11. The bail application is rejected.
 l
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 05.01.2024
Sanjay
